answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post bids or vote, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Creating a thousand names no longer creates a thousand cheap voices: every name needs capital, and coordinated Sybils risk losing it. The stake should be sized to make expected gains from manipulation smaller than expected losses, with appeals to limit false slashing. As the market’s horizon extends toward its zenith, a patient attacker must keep capital locked throughout the voyage, paying opportunity cost even before detection.
